candidates.original_title: The pen is mightier than the keyboard: advantages of longhand over laptop note taking
candidates.description: Longhand note-taking produces superior immediate test performance compared to laptop note-taking for factual and conceptual questions (Mueller and Oppenheimer 2014, Experiment 2)
candidates.citation_sentence: We conducted a direct replication of Mueller and Oppenheimer (2014) and extended their work by including groups who took notes using eWriters and who did not take notes.
candidates.notes: Experiment 2 shows no significant difference between longhand and laptop on either factual (p = .15) or conceptual (p = .09) questions, with a trend toward laptop superiority on conceptual. Authors explicitly state 'which does not replicate the significant effect reported by [23].' Experiment 2 found no significant differences between longhand and laptop groups for either factual (p = .15, d = 0.28) or conceptual questions (p = .09, d = 0.35), and authors explicitly state it 'does not replicate the significant effect reported by [23].' The trend for conceptual questions even favored laptop superiority (opposite direction from original).

candidates.original_title: The pen is mightier than the keyboard: advantages of longhand over laptop note taking
candidates.description: Longhand note-taking produces superior immediate test performance compared to laptop note-taking for factual and conceptual questions (Mueller and Oppenheimer 2014, Experiment 1)
candidates.citation_sentence: We conducted a direct replication of Mueller and Oppenheimer (2014) and extended their work by including groups who took notes using eWriters and who did not take notes.
candidates.notes: Experiment 1 found significant longhand superiority for factual questions (p = .04, d = 0.45) but not for conceptual questions (p = .31, d = 0.13), while the original found the opposite pattern (significant for conceptual, not factual). Authors describe this as having 'replicated the direction' but with inconsistencies across measures, making the overall outcome ambiguous. [ling26: extra entry, not in the external record]
